claims.text: Security / authz on every new entry point: POST /api/compare and /compare go through the workspace's shared Host, Origin and token check (server._handle before routing). A new test shows 403 for no token, a wrong token, a foreign Origin and a foreign Host, 405 for GET, and no case-log entry written.

Security / input validated at the boundary: the underwriter's figure is read exactly (at most 40 characters, digits and one point only, pence for money with no fraction of a penny and below the £10,000,000,000,000 limit), extra keys are refused, and refusals echo no input. Case text is escaped in the HTML (R34). No new dependency, secret or interpolation.

Failure modes / idempotency: a comparison writes nothing. The case log and the file list are unchanged after three comparisons. A case whose figures are refused shows no comparison. An unexpected failure now answers 500 'The figure could not be compared.' (previously 'The change could not be saved.') and doesn't repeat the error's text.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q tests/test_compare.py -k 'writes_nothing or figures_are_refused or fails_unforeseen'

claims.text: Data / migrations: not applicable. The change adds no stored field, log event, file format or migration, because the comparison is read-only and computed on request.
claims.proof_output: README.md, src/cma/indicators.py, src/cma/metrics.py, src/cma/review/compare.py, src/cma/review/server.py, tests/test_compare.py, tests/test_workspace_summary.py; no stored schema or migration file touched

claims.text: Correctness (R51, R2): the difference (yours less the tool's) is exact to the penny for any typed figure in ±£10,000,000,000,000. Other units are compared exactly as decimals, and an n/a figure has no difference. Listed lines (cash deposits, unexplained, possible own-account transfers, overridden) match an oracle built separately from the build, largest first, for a memo field, a month, each account and the combined case.

Performance: comparison_lines is one pass over the statement, with no N+1 queries. I measured one comparison on a 10,000-line case at 0.33s, listing 6,666 lines, within R52's 2-second target. The runner does not time this; my own script measured it.
Whole suite and static checks after the hardening change.

claims.text: Operability / rollback: no flag is needed. The entry is a new read-only path, and rollback is a reinstall of the previous wheel, which leaves no data to repair since nothing is stored.

notes: Gaps for the owner (design, not code): (1) Payload size / pagination: the comparison lists every flagged line in the period, 6,666 on a 10,000-line case. The design says workspace lines are paged, but the drill-down does not page either, so paging is a workspace-wide decision. (2) Observability: a comparison writes no case-log event and no structured log line, so no signal proves it ran. That matches 'nothing is saved'; whether read-only workspace actions should leave a trace is the owner's call. No alert applies because there is no remote alerting by design. (3) The 10,000-line timing is my own measurement, not a runner tier. (4) No manual browser run was done; the page and data paths are exercised through a real server in the tests.
